fixes.explanation: I can see the appeal, baker. A big showdown with folding chairs and a microphone. But that's not what Paul writes. He says, "Turn away from such as these!" (2 Timothy 3:5). That's a turn, not a debate.

Yes, baker! Paul says they are "…always learning but never able to come to a knowledge of the truth." (2 Timothy 3:7). That's a baker who keeps taking classes on oven temperatures and still never gets a batch to come out right. All that learning, and the truth never lands. Paul names that gap and doesn't soften it.

Oh, I wish I could give you that one, baker. Paul says nothing about brilliance. He says they are "…depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith." (2 Timothy 3:8). Their minds are described as depraved, not brilliant.

You got it, baker. Paul says these men "…are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith." (2 Timothy 3:8). He says it right after saying they oppose the truth. It's a serious line, and Paul states it plainly.
Yes, baker! Paul says, "But they will not advance much further." (2 Timothy 3:9). These men have a limit. They're not climbing forever, and Paul says so right there in the verse.

Baked right, baker! Paul says "…their folly will be plain to everyone." (2 Timothy 3:9). He says it will be plain, just like it was with Jannes and Jambres. Everyone will see it. That's the kind of ending that makes me smile.

That one has it backward, baker. Paul says "…their folly will be plain to everyone." (2 Timothy 3:9). It won't be unknown to everyone. It will be out where everybody can see it, just like with Jannes and Jambres. The word is plain.

Pleasing? Oh, friend, I wish. But Paul says "…their folly will be plain to everyone." (2 Timothy 3:9). The word isn't pleasing. Paul says it will be plain for all to see, just like Jannes and Jambres.
